added_failures_source: by-id set difference (head minus base) over pytest node ids read from the reviewed run's own gate logs named in its manifest: gate-logs/new-tests-base.log vs gate-logs/new-tests-head.log and gate-logs/state-typing-base.log vs gate-logs/state-typing-head.log; empty in both readings

findings.text: the mid-rewrite tolerance reads `_MANIFEST_SIZES_READ`, a process-global memory keyed by manifest path that is written only on a successful parse (:3445) and never invalidated, so a path that earlier carried a larger readable manifest suppresses the unwritten reading for as long as the file stays unreadable and smaller — with no expiry, since the size arm is checked after the mtime window and the entry is only rewritten by a parse that by assumption keeps failing; a retry that reuses its run directory's manifest.md, which is the shape the reviewed run's own directory shows, inherits the predecessor's size, so a genuinely unwritten run reads running with no expiry, and none of the four cases exercises a path whose size memory was seeded by an earlier manifest.

`_MANIFEST_SIZES_READ` grows without bound: one entry per distinct manifest path the process has ever classified, never evicted, in the follower and the watch producer, which run for days and classify every run on the workstation, so the memory is proportional to the runs ever seen rather than to the live fleet.

item_verdicts.diff: read both commits against base 99455576 — 77f56a7c adds the two windows (reckon/crew/recovery.py:107, :112), the size memory (:116, :3445), the three helpers (:3336-3401) and the gate (:3664-3667), and 3f4881dc lands the record, the figure and the plan note. The change is reader-side only, as the fence requires; the one behaviour it adds past base is at :3664-3667, where an unparseable live manifest past both windows is newly called unwritten (at base an unparseable manifest read running, which is why three of the four cases pass vacuously at base) and :3748 then points that state at `reckon crew observe` rather than at a status line that does not exist.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when's transient states are asserted by driving the classifier itself — launch window at tests/test_a_run_in_motion_is_not_unwritten.py:120-122 (live run dispatched 30 s ago, orientation-only manifest, every crew directory pointed at tmp_path through RECKON_HOME), mid-rewrite at :149-150 (4-byte unparseable manifest, mtime 1 s) and :176 (same, mtime settled, smaller than the last readable read) — and the case past the grace keeps the word at :199; the recorded head gate is 4 passed (gate-logs/new-tests-head.log) and my re-run at 3f4881dc in a scratch extraction reproduced it with the module under test resolving to /tmp/rev-3f4881dc/tree/reckon/crew/recovery.py.
item_verdicts.goal: the goal is to stop the classifier calling a live run unwritten inside its launch window or mid-rewrite of its manifest; at 3f4881dc the reading is cleared through `_absence_of_a_verdict_is_transient` (reckon/crew/recovery.py:3389) at the gate on reckon/crew/recovery.py:3664-3667, before the unwritten arm can publish it, and the four cases in tests/test_a_run_in_motion_is_not_unwritten.py pass at the reviewed head in my own re-run (4 passed, logs/reviewer-rerun-head.log) while case 1 reddens at the base revision (gate-logs/new-tests-base.log) — the two windows are exactly the states the goal names.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records the head gate (4 passed), the base arm (1 failed, 3 passed, the red being the launch-window flicker itself), the declared mutation (3 failed, 1 passed), 92 passed in tests/test_crew_recovery.py at both revisions and the sibling set at 3 pre-existing failures with 0 added; it discloses under `blockers` that the fence's third case was implemented for a manifest that is present and carries no readable verdict rather than for an absent one, because extending the word to an absent manifest took the stall arm's state. Its `baseline_suite` and `after_suite` fields are prose rather than the armed JSON shape, so a reader deriving the suite delta mechanically finds no log path there and reports the count unmeasured; I read the run's gate-logs directly instead.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the reviewed manifest declares reckon/crew/recovery.py, tests/test_a_run_in_motion_is_not_unwritten.py, docs/evidence/archive/the-fleet-counters-count-the-fleet-landed.html, docs/figures/the-fleet-counters-count-the-fleet and docs/plans/the-fleet-counters-count-the-fleet.html; `git diff --name-only 99455576 3f4881dc` returns exactly those five paths and nothing else.

justifications.durability: each case names the code change that would redden it — removing the launch window fails :120 (measured at base, 1 failed in gate-logs/new-tests-base.log) and forcing `_absence_of_a_verdict_is_transient` False fails :120, :149 and :176 (3 failed, 1 passed in negative-control.log) — and the assertions compare the returned classification to literals rather than to what the test fed in; the deductions are that :176 names only what the reading must not be (a regression to a third word would pass it) and that the size memory the tolerance keeps at :3445 can suppress the reading past any window, which no case exercises.
justifications.evidence: every result the done_when names is recorded with its log and the gate logs were kept under the run directory (gate-logs/new-tests-head.log, gate-logs/new-tests-base.log, negative-control.log), and the declared mutation's first line repeats the declaration verbatim; the production flicker is reproduced hermetically rather than on the fleet, and the base arm leaves three of four tests green for the reason the manifest itself discloses.
justifications.fit: the helpers and constants sit in the module's existing idiom (the constant block at reckon/crew/recovery.py:107-116, private helpers with mechanism-stating docstrings at :3336-3401) and introduce no name the repository's naming rules forbid; the process-global mutable cache at :116 is the one place the change departs from the module's usual explicit state.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/recovery.py:3664-3667 holds the word back in the launch window and the rewrite window and publishes it past both, which is the goal exactly; the deduction is the widening beside it, where an unparseable manifest past the windows is newly called unwritten, which the goal does not state but the word's purpose needs.
justifications.scope_discipline: `git diff --name-only 99455576 3f4881dc` lists only the five declared paths, the classifier is the only production file touched, and the writer-side half of the followup item (atomic manifest writes), which the goal does not imply, is correctly left unbuilt.
